items.title: 亦敵亦友：澳洲如何在超級大國競爭中找平衡？
items.description: 澳洲越來越擔心中國的軍事實力——但北京也是其最大的貿易夥伴。
items.content:
亦敵亦友：澳洲如何在超級大國競爭中找平衡？
  - Author, 凱蒂·沃特森（Katy Watson）
  - Role, BBC駐澳洲記者
  - Reporting from, 北昆士蘭湯斯維爾報導
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
狙擊手的槍聲打破澳洲叢林的寂靜。導彈擊中目標，遠處升起煙霧。無人機開始嗡嗡作響，但很快又被頭頂飛過的直升機聲蓋過。
各種軍事裝備悉數投入使用，不惜一切代價。但這裏並不是戰區——湯斯維爾（Townsville）上一次經歷戰火已經是第二次世界大戰期間。眼前是一場軍事力量展示。
澳洲陸軍准將本·麥克倫南（Brig Ben McLennan）說：「我們身處一個動盪的世界。」
「訓練一支軍隊，讓它準備應對一場比以往任何時候都更有可能發生的戰爭，（這）非常重要。」
對於一向覺得自己遠離世界其他地區所面對問題的澳洲人來說，戰爭已不再是一個抽象概念。
這個國家距離正在發生武裝衝突的地方數千英里，卻和其他地方一樣，正面對伊朗及烏克蘭局勢所帶來的連鎖影響，例如燃油價格上升及通脹加劇。
隨着中國軍事能力不斷提升，以及在太平洋地區的影響力日益擴大，澳洲對中國所代表的威脅也更加憂慮。
澳洲的應對方式是進一步加深與美國的關係。美國既是澳洲的安全盟友，也是中國的競爭對手——另一個超級大國。
但這也令澳洲陷入一個棘手的位置——因為中國的崛起，同時令中國成為澳洲最大的貿易夥伴。
這是一個大多數人都心知肚明的悖論——或許正因如此，我們受邀報導澳洲為保護自身所採取的措施，卻無人願意透露他們準備與誰作戰。
「我們正在為一場戰爭進行演練——一場最殘酷的戰爭——一場類似二戰、類似一戰的全面戰爭，」麥克倫南準將說道，當被問及敵人是誰時，他卻不願透露太多。
與美國進一步綁緊
眼前這場戰爭情境是名為「南方傑克魯」（Southern Jackaroo）的大型聯合軍事演習一部分。這是一項由澳洲、美國及日本軍隊參與的訓練計劃，旨在加強印太地區的防務合作。
美國海軍陸戰隊員凱文·希克斯（Kevin Hicks）說：「我們喜歡稱自己為美國的911應急部隊。」
而從人數來看，他們的部署準備程度比以往任何時候都高。2012年，只有約200名美國海軍陸戰隊員被派往澳洲，進行每年一次、為期6個月的部署。如今已增加至約2,500人。
只要快速閱讀澳洲《2026年國防戰略》，便很容易明白為甚麼這些數字正在增加。
文件指出：「主要大國之間的激烈競爭——主要是美國與中國之間——將會持續成為我們戰略環境的一項特徵。」
「中國目前持續進行全球規模最大的軍事擴張，但缺乏該地區所期待的透明度或戰略保證。」
軍事合作加深的不只是軍隊部署，也包括軍事基地——尤其是在澳洲北部。例如北領地的皇家澳洲空軍廷德爾基地（RAAF Tindal），已經完成升級，以支援美國遠程 B-52 轟炸機。
但美國、英國及澳洲之間的安全合作夥伴關係——「奧庫斯」（AUKUS）——向澳洲提供核動力潛艇，可能是雙方關係進一步深化的最大例子。
澳洲採取的方式，與其他中等強國有所不同。加拿大總理馬克·卡尼（Mark Carney）曾談及面對一個愈來愈不可靠的美國，中等強國需要重新調整優先事項；但澳洲似乎正準備與美國綁得更加緊密。
然而，與此同時，澳洲人自己對美國的關係也愈來愈存疑。
洛伊國際政策研究所（Lowy Institute）研究員查爾斯·萊昂斯—瓊斯（Charles Lyons-Jones）引用該研究所年度民調說：「只有31%的澳洲人相信美國會在世界上負責任地行事，而相信中國會如此行事的澳洲人更只有28%。」
「當你考慮到澳洲政府對美國的信任程度時，這些結果尤其令人矚目。」
「亦敵亦友」
澳洲與美國的盟友關係正在改變，而澳洲與中國的關係也一樣。
軍隊可能正在為潛在的軍事衝突作準備，但事實仍然是，中國是澳洲最重要的經濟夥伴。
澳洲與中國自1972年起建立外交關係，但直到2010年代初，中國才成為澳洲最大的貿易夥伴，當時中國對澳洲提供的各種商品需求龐大。
澳洲開放經濟，鼓勵商業及貿易；中國國家主席習近平更獲邀在澳洲國會發表演說。最終，雙方在2015年簽署自由貿易協定。
但這段黃金時期並沒有持續太久。2020年，澳洲提出調查新冠疫情的起源，中國反對這一調查方向，並以關稅作為反制。
到了2021年，澳洲成為第一個在「一帶一路」倡議問題上作出政策逆轉的國家。中國的「一帶一路」是一項大規模全球基礎設施計劃；澳洲政府在與中國政府簽署協議3年後，取消了維多利亞州與中國政府達成的相關協議。
也有多名澳洲人在中國遭到拘留，其中包括記者成蕾。她在被拘留超過3年後，於2023年獲釋。
近年來，在總理阿爾巴尼斯（Anthony Albanese；艾巴尼斯）領導的工黨政府下，兩國關係有所改善，但仍然存在挑戰。
例如今年6月，中國以保護本土市場，對澳洲牛肉徵收55%關稅——儘管雙方已簽署自由貿易協定。
即使存在這些波折，洛伊研究所今年的民調發現，大多數澳洲人（61%）仍然認為中國更像是一個經濟夥伴，而不是安全威脅。這個比例較去年增加11個百分點。
不過，談到中國在澳洲投資時，澳洲人則更加謹慎。
萊昂斯—瓊斯說：「有一些歐洲國家在澳洲的投資規模比中國更大，這是因為我們的司法管轄制度更加相似，而且兩國政府之間的互信程度也更高。」
洛伊研究所今年的民調還顯示，首次有過半數澳洲人（51%）認為，澳洲與中國的關係，比澳洲與美國的關係更重要。
超級大國的興衰
本月較早時，前澳洲總理陸克文（Kevin Rudd）——一名能流利說普通話的人——發表演說，談到正在重新塑造澳洲國家安全形勢的「劇烈變化」，其中包括「中國不斷崛起之際，美國仍在持續辯論自己希望成為一個怎樣的全球大國」。
悉尼科技大學（University of Technology Sydney）副教授張越（Marina Yue Zhang）認為，澳洲與其最親密盟友的關係正在改變。
她說：「美國確實正在做一些非常重大的改變，而愈來愈多澳洲人——我認為全球也有愈來愈多人——已經開始問：『這是我們所有人都可以信任、並寄予全部信任的那個大哥嗎？』」
但昔日的競爭仍然存在。澳洲夾在兩個超級大國之間，兩國領導人之間的每一次互動都具有重要意義。
今年稍早在北京，習近平與特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）會面時，中國國家主席提到「修昔底德陷阱」（Thucydides Trap）這一概念——這一理論認為，當一個崛起中的大國挑戰一個既有大國時，衝突可能變得幾乎不可避免。
張越說：「這是——如果不是大國之間的權力轉移，至少也是大國之間的權力鬥爭。」
而在這場競爭中，澳洲不可避免地受到影響。美國是澳洲的安全盟友，儘管相比過去變得更加不可靠，但仍然是澳洲的主要依靠。
但在經濟上，中國同樣如此。這並不是一個非此即彼的關係，而是一場平衡。
張越說：「澳洲不可能選擇其中一方而（拋棄）另一方——這不符合澳洲的利益。」
「要維持這種平衡正變得愈來愈困難，但澳洲必須這樣做。」

items.title: 美國檢方重啟調查康奈爾大學輪姦案指控
items.description: 此前，一名女子提起民事訴訟，聲稱她在2024年於一所兄弟會會所被下藥並遭到強姦。
items.content:
美國檢方重啟調查康奈爾大學輪姦案指控
  - Author, 凱拉·愛潑斯坦（Kayla Epstein）、納爾丁·薩阿德（Nardine Saad）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
美國紐約州檢察官表示，他們將就2024年康奈爾大學（Cornell University）一名女子涉嫌遭強姦案重啟刑事調查。
該女子於今年9月16日提出民事訴訟，指控自己在這所大學一間兄弟會會所（fraternity house）內被下藥，並遭多人強姦。
湯普金斯縣（Tompkins County）地方檢察官馬修·范·豪頓（Matthew Van Houten）週一（28日）表示：「一旦我們確定適當的控罪，案件將透過大陪審團，以最客觀和公正的方式檢控。」
康奈爾大學表示，雖然校方支持將案件提交大陪審團審理，但「任何暗示大學沒有對涉事人士施加具實質影響的懲罰的說法，都是錯誤的」。
該女子在法庭文件中以珍·杜（Jane Doe；女性無名氏）代稱。她在訴訟中指稱，2024年10月19日晚，康奈爾大學 Chi Phi 兄弟會分會的7名男子涉嫌將其性侵，事件涉及酒精及氯胺酮。
Jane Doe 在訴訟中表示，事發期間她處於醉酒狀態，無法表達同意。
她說，自己於2024年11月8日向康奈爾大學警察報案。
訴訟文件亦附有一張據稱來自兄弟會 Snapchat 群組聊天的截圖，當中一名參與者以粗俗字眼提醒其他成員，指他們可能有機會與 Jane Doe 發生性接觸。
范·豪頓週一表示，在兩年前事件發生後，他的辦公室認為，Jane Doe 向當局作出的陳述所提供的證據，未達到提出刑事控罪的法律門檻。
他說，在準備將案件提交大陪審團期間，他主動聯絡 Jane Doe 及其律師要求提供更多資料。
在美國法律制度下，檢察官會召集大陪審團，審視證據及證詞，最終由陪審團投票決定有關證據是否足以提出刑事檢控。
范·豪頓在聲明中概述了 Jane Doe 於2024年涉嫌遭襲後向康奈爾大學警察部門作出的陳述。他指出這份陳述與民事訴訟中的指控有所不同。
范·豪頓週一在聲明中說：「Jane Doe 在2024年11月作出的宣誓陳述，並沒有指稱自己遭人強行下藥，亦沒有指稱自己遭多人強姦。」
「相反，Jane Doe 的陳述描述她參與吸食毒品及性行為時，是自願、清醒並同意的。」
范·豪頓又說，Jane Doe 的律師從未聯絡他，表示她最初的陳述並不準確，也從未要求他重新考慮不提出控罪的決定。
他其後承認，「現實是性侵受害者可能需要多年的治療和療癒，才能充分處理及理解發生在自己身上的事情」。
BBC 已聯絡 Jane Doe 的律師托馬斯·朱弗拉（Thomas Giuffra）。他週一向BBC在美國的合作夥伴哥倫比亞廣播公司（CBS）發表聲明說：「在事件發生後的幾天內，（Jane Doe）受到創傷，感到麻木，無法正常生活，也無法接受所發生事情的可怕程度。她當時處於自我保護狀態。」
朱弗拉說，Jane Doe 除了向最初接報的警員陳述外，從未再向其他人談及事件。他說：「至少，我原本預期她會接受警方多次盤問，執法人員會收集證據，並逐步建立案件。這是嚴重刑事案件調查的正常程序。」
他說：「我從地方檢察官的聲明中感受到的防衛姿態，令我相信他們意識到當中存在失誤，並正試圖為這些失誤找藉口。」
Jane Doe 亦在民事訴訟中指稱，康奈爾大學沒有保護她，也沒有對涉事男子作出足夠懲罰。她指稱，涉事男子「獲提供機會透過提交文章來減輕其行為所受到的處分」。
訴訟文件指出，Jane Doe 因事件及大學處理事件的方式而遭受「嚴重的情緒及心理困擾，以及身體傷害」，並指事件的消息很快就在校園內傳開。
2024年11月，康奈爾大學就 Chi Phi 兄弟會會所內「有關濫用毒品及性暴力的嚴重且令人深感不安的指控」發表公開聲明，表示校方警察部門正在調查，並已暫停 Chi Phi 兄弟會當地分會以及「多名學生」的活動。
康奈爾大學亦表示，校方已展開內部調查，以及根據《第九條》（the Title IX law）進行民權調查。《第九條》禁止接受聯邦政府資助的學校，包括大部分大學在性別方面實施歧視。
週一，康奈爾大學否認 Jane Doe 所指校方沒有充分調查或懲罰涉嫌涉案人士。
大學在聲明中表示，案件已交由「由受過訓練的教職員組成的小組」處理，該小組作出「一系列處分」，包括將涉事人士逐出康奈爾大學及停學。
康奈爾大學說：「被指控的人中，沒有任何人僅僅因為參與事件就被給予撰寫文章的機會。」
訴訟中其中一名被點名男子的律師傑里米·薩蘭德（Jeremy Saland）否認有關指控。
薩蘭德承認，他的當事人「在 Snapchat 上作出回應及發表了一則不成熟的評論」，但「除此之外甚麼也沒有做」。薩蘭德否認其當事人「參與任何性行為，也沒有以任何方式接觸原告，亦沒有服用氯胺酮」。
Jane Doe 提出訴訟以及案件宣布重新調查後，事件受到全國關注。包括女演員佛羅倫斯·珀（Florence Pugh；弗洛倫絲·皮尤／佛蘿倫絲·普伊／科倫絲·佩芝）在內的多名名人都曾就事件公開發聲。

items.title: 伊朗女歌手演出不戴頭巾遭判笞刑74鞭 上訴遭駁回
items.description: 帕拉斯托·阿赫瑪迪因在一場直播音樂會中身穿無袖連身裙演唱，被裁定犯有「冒犯公共道德」罪。
items.content:
伊朗女歌手演出不戴頭巾遭判笞刑74鞭 上訴遭駁回
  - Author, 貢切·哈比比亞扎德（Ghoncheh Habibiazad）
  - Role, BBC波斯語記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
伊朗律師表示，上訴法院已確認對一名未佩戴法定希賈布（hijab）頭巾表演的知名歌手判處笞刑74鞭。
帕拉斯托·阿赫瑪迪（Parastoo Ahmadi）於2024年12月在其YouTube頻道直播的一場音樂會中，身穿無袖連身裙演唱。伊朗法律禁止女性公開表演，並規定女性須佩戴頭巾及穿著端莊服裝。
這名29歲歌手的影片獲得數百萬次觀看並迅速走紅後，伊朗司法機關對她提起訴訟，稱該演出「違反國家法律及文化規範」。
據報導，庫姆（Qom）一所刑事法院於6月裁定阿赫瑪迪以及其樂隊和製作團隊的八名成員罪名成立，罪名包括透過發布「淫穢及不雅內容」而「冒犯公共道德」。
除被判處74下鞭刑外，他們還被禁止從事視聽活動，並被禁止離境兩年。
根據辯護律師的說法，上星期五（9月25日），被告提出的上訴在未經開庭審理的情況下遭上級法院「駁回」。
其中一名律師告訴BBC：「在我們看來，舉辦這場音樂會根本不構成犯罪。初審法院就這些指控判處了最嚴厲的刑罰之一，儘管也可以選擇罰款或較輕的懲罰。」
「上訴法院雖然可以選擇開庭審理，但並未開庭，而是維持原判。看來作出這項判決的主要原因，是為了阻止類似事件再次發生。」
初審判決消息傳出後，在伊朗社交媒體上引發廣泛反應。
流亡歌手 Googoosh 當時在Instagram上寫道：「願這些黑暗的日子結束，願女性重新獲得選擇自己生活方式和穿著方式的自由，願藝術表達再次在我們珍愛的祖國蓬勃發展。」
音樂家侯賽因·阿里扎德（Hossein Alizadeh）則表示，他「願意代替帕拉斯托·阿赫瑪迪承受70下鞭刑」。
人權活動人士也譴責這項判決。國際特赦組織（Amnesty International）警告說，「鞭刑構成殘忍、不人道及有辱人格的懲罰，違反絕對禁止酷刑及其他虐待的原則」。
2024年1月，庫爾德裔伊朗活動人士羅亞·赫什馬蒂（Roya Heshmati）因社交媒體上一張未佩戴頭巾的照片，被裁定「違反公共道德」，並遭鞭打74下。
據庫爾德人權組織「亨加」（Hengaw）稱，她表示，在德里黑一家檢察官辦公室內，一名女性警員強行將頭巾戴在她頭上，之後一名男性警員鞭打她的肩膀、背部、臀部及腿部。
根據伊朗法律——而該法律建基於該國對伊斯蘭教法（Sharia）的詮釋——達到青春期的女性及女孩必須以頭巾遮蓋頭髮，並穿著寬鬆長衣，以掩蓋身體曲線。
2022年，22歲庫爾德裔女性馬哈薩·阿米尼（Mahsa Amini）因被指「未妥善佩戴頭巾」，於當年9月在德里黑遭道德警察拘留後死亡，隨即引發席捲伊斯蘭共和國全國的示威浪潮。
在反對宗教統治體制的全國性示威中，女性焚燒頭巾或將其高舉揮舞。安全部隊其後展開鎮壓，造成數百人死亡。
自那時起，許多女性及女孩公開拒絕遵守服裝規範，完全不再遮蓋頭髮。當局則以一波又一波的拘捕、警告、關閉商戶及其他措施作出回應。
本月稍早談及頭巾執法問題時，保守派政治人物、國家利益委員會成員吳拉姆阿里·哈達德—阿德爾（Gholamali Haddad‑Adel）表示，由於伊朗正與美國及以色列交戰，當局「目前無法像應該做的那樣在這條戰線上投入太多精力」。他同時也是最高領袖莫傑塔巴·哈梅內伊（Mojtaba Khamenei）的岳父。
這場戰爭於2月底爆發。數星期前，伊朗安全部隊才剛剛暴力鎮壓另一波由經濟危機引發的大規模抗議活動，造成數以千計民眾死亡。

items.title: 特朗普習近平峰會：沒有說出口的議題可能更重要
items.description: 白宮峰會最耐人尋味之處，或許在於中美兩國領導人沒有說哪些事，以及我們至今仍不知道哪些事。
items.content:
特朗普習近平峰會：沒有說出口的議題可能更重要
  - Author, 碧嘉蘭（Laura Bicker）
  - Role, BBC駐中國記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
中國星期一（9月28日）公佈了更多有關國家主席習近平與唐納德·特朗普（Donald Tump；川普）上星期會談中達成共識的資訊，讓一些具體成果得以曝光。
但雙方沒有發表聯合聲明，也幾乎沒有重大突破。
相反，兩國政府各自發布了這次會晤的說法，這或許顯示儘管有白宮參觀行程以及加強雙邊關係的承諾，華盛頓與北京仍對彼此保持戒心。
以下是我們目前已知，以及仍然未知的四件有關此次會談的事情。
新的人工智能對話與溝通渠道
北京表示，已與華盛頓同意啟動新的人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧）對話機制，並安排於11月底進一步會談。
在兩國競相發展先進人工智能之際，此舉顯示雙方認為有必要為這項日益被應用於商業以至軍事規劃等領域的技術設立某種防護機制。
雙方亦同意建立一條處理人工智能事件的溝通渠道，旨在防止誤解或意外事態發展演變成更廣泛的對抗。
外界一直密切關注此次會談是否會在人工智能相關議題上出現任何進展或協議，尤其是在 Anthropic 等美國公司呼籲放慢發展步伐，以及有消息披露 OpenAI 曾未經授權存取澳洲等國家的政府網站，並曾「干預」多個美國政府機構網站之後。
貿易休戰：包括了甚麼，又遺漏了甚麼
中國官方星期一首次證實，貿易休戰已延長至1月10日。
這項短期延長確保兩位領導人將於今年稍後在主要國際會議期間再次會面。
特朗普將於11月出席在深圳舉行的亞太經濟合作組織（APEC）峰會，而習近平則預定於12月前往邁阿密出席二十國集團（G20）峰會。
世界兩大經濟體領導人如此頻繁會面並不常見。
但北京原本希望休戰安排能夠延長更久，因此這項為期兩個月的延長只能算是溫和成果，而非重大突破。
中國確實爭取到價值300億美元（2013億元人民幣；9541億元新台幣）輸美商品的較低關稅，而北京方面預計也將作出相應幅度的關稅下調。
運往美國商店的中國商品，包括玩具、小型家用電器及聖誕裝飾品等，都將受惠於較低關稅。
特朗普政府亦表示，北京將於2027年及2028年每年至少購買1000萬公噸煤炭。
引人注目的是那些未被納入的內容。
雙方沒有提及增加中國稀土礦物對美出口，也沒有任何跡象顯示對美國先進半導體的限制措施將會放寬。
美國沒有提及台灣，但中國提了
白宮的事實清單並未提及台灣，但這個議題顯然是習近平的優先事項。
根據北京方面對會談的描述，習近平敦促特朗普正式反對台灣獨立，並謹慎處理這一問題。
在雙方5月上一次會晤後，特朗普透露，習近平曾直接問他，一旦中國發動攻擊，美國是否會保衛台灣。
他向記者表示：「只有一個人知道答案，那就是我。」他並提出疑問，美軍是否有必要為此「跋涉9500英里（1.53萬公里）去打一場戰爭」。
這一次，特朗普透露的內容少得多。
他在週末向記者表示：「這個問題我們沒有談太多。」
特朗普說：「目前情況很好，一切都在推進之中。他非常了解我的想法。」
這種沉默或許具有重要意義。
特朗普此前曾形容一項擬議中的140億美元對台軍售方案，是他與北京打交道時「非常好的談判籌碼」。這項軍售方案已擱置數月。
進一步加深外界困惑的是，美國駐華大使龐德偉（David Perdue）向霍士新聞（Fox News）表示，特朗普曾在峰會期間提出向習近平出售武器。
美國國務院其後澄清，美國法律禁止向中國出售武器，且目前並無此類計劃。
北京視這個實行自治的島嶼為中國的一部分。包括美國在內的大多數國家都不承認台灣是一個獨立國家，但華盛頓反對任何以武力奪取台灣的企圖，並承諾向台灣提供武器。
中國可能正在打開投資大門
中國表示，將允許更多外國金融公司，包括有美國背景的銀行、投資公司及保險公司，申請在中國經營業務及設立辦事處。但任何批准仍須遵守中國法律法規。
最後這一句是關鍵。中國正在打開大門，但仍掌控誰可以通過。
外國金融公司長期抱怨，監管障礙、牌照要求以及對出境禁令的憂慮，令它們即使在理論上獲准進入市場的情況下，仍難以擴展在華業務。
北京還表示，正討論增加兩國之間航班數量的方法，但雙方都未說明將如何實現。
此外，儘管中國已向全球超過75個國家的訪客提供免簽證入境待遇，但並未將這項安排擴展至美國人。
與此同時，美國國務院仍把赴華旅行列為第二級旅遊警示，敦促旅客「提高警覺」，原因包括面臨任意執法、出境禁令及拘留的風險。
因此，即使雙方都在談論鼓勵商務往來和旅行，一些最大的障礙仍然牢牢存在。
那麼，我們其實都知道些甚麼？
這次峰會帶來了更多對話，但目前幾乎沒有改變任何重大決策。從先進科技到台灣等最具爭議性的議題，仍然未獲解決。
但對兩位領導人而言，這是熟悉的結果：承諾建立更多溝通渠道、作出有限的經濟讓步，以及提出溫和的穩定雙邊關係方案。
而儘管雙方都仍致力維持穩定關係，持續的美中對話似乎遠比要求任何一個超級大國作出妥協來得容易。

items.title: 在印尼一座熱帶島嶼上，備受珍視的「永恆積雪」即將永遠消失
items.description: 氣候變化正改變著印尼巴布亞長年被積雪覆蓋的山峰，而這些山峰不但具有科學價值，還有其精神意義。
items.content:
在印尼一座熱帶島嶼上，備受珍視的「永恆積雪」即將永遠消失
  - Author, 亞伯拉罕·烏塔馬（Abraham Utama）
  - Role, BBC印尼語記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
巴布亞（Papua）的山脈距離赤道（equator）不遠，但數百年來山頂一直覆蓋着「永恆積雪」。
這個位於全球第二大島嶼、澳洲以北的印尼地區，其山峰為科學家提供了無數有關地球氣候歷史的見解。
對許多巴布亞人來說，這些山峰亦是其精神世界的核心。有活動人士形容，這就像麥加或梵蒂岡一樣。
但如今，幾乎所有積雪都已消失。
一個世紀前，綿延300公里（190英里）的蘇迪曼山脈（Sudirman Range）四座主要山峰上都覆蓋着積雪和永久冰層。
但如今，只有查亞峰（Puncak Jaya）——亦稱卡斯滕斯金字塔（Carstensz Pyramid）——周圍仍存有少量積雪，並預計在一兩年內完全消失。
峰頂周圍的冰川覆蓋面積，已由19世紀約1900公頃（4700英畝）縮減至現今約16公頃（40英畝）。幾乎整座冰川都在人類一生之內消失殆盡。
捷克冰川生態學家瑪麗·沙巴茨卡（Marie Šabacká）說：「這當中存在着深刻的不公平。」她於去年3月前往查亞峰，希望成為最後一批研究巴布亞「永恆積雪」的科學家之一。
她表示，巴布亞的熱帶冰川極為獨特，因為它們與其他冰川系統相隔數千公里。巴布亞擁有安第斯山脈與喜馬拉雅山脈之間「最後殘存的熱帶冰層」。
從查亞峰山坡鑽取的冰芯保存着氣候歷史的紀錄。
科學家可利用這些冰芯獲取該地區大氣狀況的資訊，並了解環繞島嶼——即熱帶太平洋和西太平洋暖池（the tropical Pacific and Western Pacific Warm pool）——這片地球最溫暖海域的變化。
但在科學家有時間全面研究之前，這份檔案正逐漸消失。
全球暖化的證據
沙巴茨卡指出，巴布亞冰川消退的原因，與全球其他地方冰層融化的原因相同，即由人類活動造成的大氣暖化，包括燃燒煤炭、石油和天然氣等化石燃料。
隨着氣溫上升，冰點會向山體更高處移動，因此更多降水會以雨水而非降雪形式出現，即使是在過去經常降雪的地方也是如此。
厄爾尼諾現象（El Niño；聖嬰現象）可能加速這一過程，而雲層覆蓋、降雪量和山體地形等當地因素則會影響其速度。
沙巴茨卡表示，巴布亞的山脈位於赤道以南僅450公里（280英里）處，「永久冰層只能在極高海拔及狹窄的氣候條件範圍內存續」。
她補充說，氣溫略微上升、冰點提高，或由降雪轉為降雨，都可能決定冰川是否能夠存續。
冰川退縮是地球長期暖化的證據，而其消失「既抹去了一個生物棲息地，也抹去了一部分具有重要文化意義的景觀」。
精神支柱
至少有五個原住民族群世世代代都與查亞峰有深厚的精神聯繫。
莫尼族（Moni）稱其為「Mbainggela」，並相信祖先守護着這座山；對阿蒙梅族（Amungme）而言，這片山脈被稱為「Nemangkawi」，即「白箭」。
年輕的阿蒙梅族女性埃爾弗里達·納特基梅（Elfrida Natkime）說：「父母和祖父母會祈求孩子擁有如白箭般的心靈，永不偏離正道。它象徵誠實、純潔和道德正直。」
按照阿蒙梅族的傳統信仰，「Nemangkawi」象徵人們應如何生活。
阿蒙梅族環保活動人士阿道菲娜·庫姆（Adolfina Kum）強調，這座山峰對她的族人有多麼重要，以及隨着冰川融化，傳統與文化根基面臨被摧毀的風險。
她問道：「如果麥加被毀，穆斯林會有甚麼感受？如果羅馬或梵蒂岡被毀，天主教徒又會有甚麼感受？對阿蒙梅族人來說，『Nemangkawi』被摧毀時就是這種感受。」
對許多巴布亞原住民而言，冰川消失並非孤立事件。
大量銅礦和金礦礦藏的發現，在20世紀改變了這個地區，而資源開採工業項目的發展亦重塑了部分地貌。
整片山體被開挖，道路、工業基礎設施和聚居地改變了周邊山谷的面貌。
巴布亞人表示，這些開發帶來了就業機會、道路、教育和經濟發展機遇，但同時也造成環境惡化及持續數十年的社會衝突。隨着採礦活動擴張，一些人失去了進入祖傳土地的權利。
BBC已聯絡營運巴布亞格拉斯伯格礦場（Grasberg mine）的自由港公司（Freeport）尋求回應。該礦場是全球最大的金礦和銅礦業務之一。
埃爾弗里達·納特基梅說：「每當我看到這些山脈，我都感到驚歎，但也感到悲傷⋯⋯自從那家公司進駐以來，我看到了開採活動。但這些發展也為許多人提供了生計。」
當地社群目睹其神聖景觀發生變化之際，科學家和探險家正爭分奪秒記錄仍然留存的一切。
丹麥研究員克勞斯·蒂曼（Klaus Thymann）及其團隊利用無人機和三維測繪技術，建立了現存冰川的詳細模型。
他表示，從2000年代初至2025年，冰川覆蓋區域已縮減95%。「幾乎已經沒有冰了。這就是事實。」
蒂曼表示，冰川作為氣候變化指標「具有令人難以置信的力量」。
他解釋說：「當人們聽到某些被形容為『永恆』的事物正在消失時，就會產生反應。」
阿道菲娜·庫姆認為，當神聖山脈、森林或祖先之地受到破壞時，社群便會「失去重要的力量來源」。
「我常把這形容為把一棵樹連根拔起。沒了根，樹木便失去了基礎。」

items.title: 《商报》：德国政府拟阻止中远海运收购物流企业Zippel
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/《商报》：德国政府拟阻止中远海运收购物流企业zippel/a-79476866?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 德国联邦政府据报计划阻止中远海运收购德国物流公司Zippel。《商报》援引一份政府内部文件称存在“重大安全顾虑”，担心交易或使德国在关键物流节点形成战略依赖并在政治冲突中被用作施压手段。最终决定尚未作出，但据报道多个联邦部门均反对该笔交易。
items.content:
《商报》：德国政府拟阻止中远海运收购物流企业Zippel
2026年9月29日
（德国之声中文网）据德国《商报》（Handelsblatt）报道，德国联邦政府计划禁止中远海运收购物流企业Zippel。该消息源自《商报》查阅的一份政府内部备忘录，文件中提到存在“重大安全顾虑”。最终决定尚未作出，但知情人士预计结果或对中远海运不利。
中远海运发言人周二（9月29日）向路透社表示，在最终决定作出之前，公司不愿对此发表评论。Zippel和德国经济部当均未作出回应。
担忧战略依赖被用作施压工具
据《商报》报道，全球第四大航运公司计划收购Zippel公司80%的股份。
汉堡的货运代理公司Konrad Zippel主要从事海陆联运业务，将内陆的卡车运输、铁路运输与远洋货轮连接起来。货物主要从北海港口运往德国东部。尽管市场份额不大，但其业务集中在德国东部，正是这一地理业务布局引发了柏林方面对收购案的反对。
据《商报》看到的文件，Zippel在柏林、施科保（Schkopau）和埃尔斯特韦尔达（Elsterwerda）三个货运站的货物处理量占比在35%到90%之间。文件指出，这可能造成战略依赖 - 在政治关系出现动荡时，这种依赖可能被用作施压工具。
此外，相关担忧还涉及对德国联邦国防军的后勤支持。一旦发生冲突，通往德国东部边境的物流运输对北约而言也至关重要。
与码头案不同：各部委一致反对收购
在德国汉堡港，中远集团也曾在2022年收购了“福地”(Tollerort)集装箱码头的24.9%股份。尽管各界普遍担忧北京会因此获得过大的对关键基础设施的影响力、加深德国对中国的经济依赖度，时任总理肖尔茨依然力推准许这笔交易。德国联邦政府经过长期争论于2023年5月批准中方入股，但将持股比例限制在25%以下，以防其获得足以阻止重大股东决议的少数表决权。当时，反对这一投资的声音主要来自由绿党领导的经济部。
据《商报》报道，此次中远海运计划收购Zippel股权案，不仅是经济部，外交部、国防部、内政部和财政部也都希望阻止该交易。欧盟委员会也曾就该收购案向德国经济部发出警告。
今年4月底，德广联调查披露称，德国联邦宪法保卫局已经在内部明确反对中远收购Zippel，理由是中远集团在欧洲的“累积性收购行为”可能导致这家中国国有航运巨头的进一步战略扩张。所谓“累积性收购”，指的是多个看似单独分散的投资实际上都服务于国家的整体长期战略。
截至周二，路透社记者暂未能联系到Zippel总经理阿克塞尔·普拉斯（Axel Plaß）置评。
普拉斯在接受《德国交通报》（Deutsche Verkehrs-Zeitung）采访时表示，德国联邦卡特尔局批准交易后，经济部在投资审查程序中启动了第二轮审查。他说，进一步审查涉及的问题包括Zippel的软件架构情况，以及公司是否处理敏感数据等问题。
普拉斯表示：“我们通常并不知道集装箱里装的是什么，因为我们只是供应链中的一个小环节。”他还称，公司的IT架构源自德国和欧洲。
他最后表示：“Zippel的市场份额约为1.5%，不值得引起如此大的公众舆论关注。”

items.title: 全球创新指数排行榜出炉：中国第10、德国第11
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/全球创新指数排行榜出炉：中国第10、德国第11/a-79476680?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 去年德国被踢出全球创新指数前十国家，今年德国继续保持了第11名的这个位置。中国则在去年首次跻身前十，今年也得以保持。拔得头筹的仍然是瑞士。
items.content:
全球创新指数排行榜出炉：中国第10、德国第11
2026年9月29日
（德国之声中文网）联合国世界知识产权组织（WIPO）最新的创新指数出炉，德国的排名保持了去年的位置：第11名，较2022年获得的最好排名第8位有所下滑。
中国排位第10。在去年的排名中，中国首次进入创新最佳的前十大经济体之列。在35个中高收入经济体中，中国排名第一。中高收入经济体指人均GDP在4636–14375美元之间的国家与地区。在亚洲，中国仅次于韩国和新加坡。近年来，中国的创新排名不断跃升。
2026年最具创新力的前10国家分别是瑞士、瑞典、美国、韩国、新加坡、英国、荷兰、芬兰、丹麦和中国。
世界知识产权组织对139个国家的约80项指标进行评估，涵盖的范围包括研发、高科技贸易、技术岗位和知识产权许可等各个方面。
德国数字信息技术应用落后
正如位于慕尼黑的德国专利商标局强调的那样，该指数显示德国拥有健全的创新体系，然而，它也指出，在一些对经济发展至关重要的指标上，德国的表现明显逊于大多数排名靠前的国家。
在数字信息技术应用方面，德国仅排名第60位，比去年下降了3位。德国的外国直接投资流入量排名第94位。在文化与促进创业的措施指标中，德国排名第36位。这里文化指的是，促进或阻碍创业活动的社会和文化规范。德国在人力资本和研发（第3）以及工程专业毕业生比例（第5）等领域得分较高。
WIPO的报告指出，人工智能正在推动风险投资的使用：2025年，对创新型初创企业和商业理念的投资总额增长了28%，达到5100亿美元。这是自2021年以来最强劲的年度增长。
人工智能领域占全球风险投资的53%，2026年上半年，这一比例更是达到77%。WIPO预测，今年全球研发支出预计将增长3.6%，达到3.4万亿美元。
创新集群：中国第一、德国第三
同去年一样，本次报告也公布了“创新集群”（innovation clusters）100强的排名，前10名分别是：深圳-香港-广州再占鳌头，接下来是东京-横板、圣何塞—旧金山、北京、首尔、上海—苏州、纽约、伦敦、波士顿—剑桥、大阪—神户—京都。
中国共有25个创新集群进入全球前100，全球最多；德国有 7个，排名全球第3，仅次于中国和美国（20）。

items.title: 德语媒体：休战期延长 火药味未减
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：休战期延长-火药味未减/a-79476387?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 《新苏黎世报》评论写道，中美峰会上，两国领导人笑逐颜开的姿态无法掩盖中美之间的深层矛盾，两个月的“休战期”过后，全球经济仍需面对贸易战死灰复燃的风险。《南德意志报》评论称，特朗普对习近平的极力讨好也显示出，华盛顿已经无法承受公开对抗中国的代价。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）《新苏黎世报》评论写道，此次特习会虽然场面宏大，但值得一提的成果却只是贸易“休战”状态得以暂时维持。但只要中美贸易冲突的根源不能排除，贸易战也就随时都可能全面爆发。这篇题为《鹅肝酱取代不了自由贸易》的评论写道：
“中美新的关税协定充其量只能勉强起到遮羞布的作用。今年五月的特习会之后，双方贸易代表一直在就价值六百亿美元、不涉及国家安全的非敏感产品进行讨价还价。而最终的谈判结果仅仅覆盖了双边贸易的极小一部分，具体内容更是令人啼笑皆非：中方降低了对美国进口鹅肝酱的关税，而作为回报，美方也将减少中国进口手电筒和电熨斗的关税。
核心问题和重要商品都没有被涉及。真正能让中国经济从中受益的，并非来自美国的鹅肝酱，而是美国的计算机芯片。而美国迫切需要的，并不是廉价的中国手电筒，而是磁铁和稀土。美方认为，中国供应的磁体数量少于2025年双方的约定，此外，中方有关购买更多美国玉米和谷物的承诺迄今也仍未兑现。
尽管此次特习会的场面宏大，表面上看起来也是一团和气，但两国对各自国际地位以及全球贸易体系的不同看法仍表现得非常突出。习近平在华盛顿表示，中美两国间完全可以避免陷入‘修昔底德陷阱’。这个以古希腊历史学家命名的典故，是指一个高度自信的崛起大国同一个疑虑重重的衰落大国之间必将发生冲突。”
表面上看起来，这似乎是以乐观心态看待中美关系的前景。但对特朗普来说，这其实更像是一种侮辱。习近平是在说中国已经走上了赶超美国的道路，因此理应获得不同以往的国际地位。但在特朗普眼中，美国正处在‘黄金时代’，绝不是一个应当让位的衰落大国。”
《新苏黎世报》评论写道，此次特习会表现出一派融洽氛围，这固然是件好事。但中美领导人间的融洽关系并不足以稳固两国关系，更不足以避免双边贸易战的死灰复燃：
“两位领导人只将贸易‘休战期’延长了两个月，足以说明一切。特朗普希望在11月初的中期选举前一切风平浪静，但也保留了选举后重启战火的选项。而北京也为随时采取反制措施做好了准备。总而言之，几箱鹅肝酱无法掩盖贸易战死灰复燃的风险。而中美贸易战一旦爆发，世界其他193个国家势必都会遭殃。”
“特朗普迫切希望获得习近平的认可”
上周，美国总统特朗普亲赴机场迎接中国国家主席习近平到访。欢迎仪式上，当一架B-2轰炸机轰鸣着掠过中美领导人的头顶，特朗普眉头紧蹙，习近平则面无表情。《南德意志报》评论写道，一场精心策划的实力秀，反而成了暴露软弱的瞬间：
“今年中美领导人直接会面的频率高得离奇。对中方来说，理由很简单：北京不必担心习近平会像乌克兰总统泽连斯基一样，遭到特朗普的当众羞辱。对习来说，这本身就是美国示弱的表现：华盛顿已经无法承受同中国公开对抗的代价，而北京也乐得向世人展示这一点。
特朗普只字不提中方向伊朗提供军民两用品的问题，这些物资有可能会被用来生产无人机和导弹；只字不提北京对俄罗斯侵乌战争提供的帮助；更只字不提中国对邻邦发出的威胁。无论是台湾，还是日本，都已经一头雾水，几乎搞不清楚美国究竟是伙伴，还是风险。相反，习近平却在美国获得了最高级别的礼遇：数百名美国士兵列队欢迎，特朗普则对‘美好真挚的友谊’赞不绝口。特朗普显然已经无法掩饰自己获得习近平认可的迫切心情。面对习近平，他会本能地做出卑躬屈膝的姿态。
然而，同此前的历次特习会一样，此次中美峰会既没有促成双方的结盟，更没有带来双边关系的靠拢。特朗普或许认为自己是个交易大师，但中方却从未这样想过。习近平认为，中国正置身一场大国博弈，而这场博弈中，信任是一种示弱的表现。与此同时，他还担心，美国会试图推翻中国的现行政治制度。中美难以建立起信任的另一个障碍则是：特朗普虽然一直坚持对威权统治者的敬佩和崇拜，但其他方面却变幻无常、难以预测。”

items.title: 长平观察：特朗普用人民大会堂来羞辱白宫
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/长平观察：特朗普用人民大会堂来羞辱白宫/a-79473485?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 特朗普多次表示把人民大会堂当作白宫新宴会厅的灵感和竞争对象。时事评论作家长平指出，威权统治者常用宏大建筑制造权力的永久感和敬畏感。假如希特勒的人民大厅得以建成，特朗普灵感来源就轮不到北京了。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）上周四（9月24日），习近平访问白宫的第一个完整日，特朗普带他看了两处工地：拆除东翼后在建的宴会厅，和本周启用的直升机停机坪。
据《纽约时报》报道，记者们一路喊问伊朗、台湾和黎智英，两人都没回应。特朗普只说了一句：“他精通很多领域，还是石材专家，特别喜欢上好的花岗岩。”据白宫记者团描述，习近平面无表情，一言不发。
在拆除东翼的争议中，特朗普近几个月至少六次公开称赞北京人民大会堂，称它是宴会厅的灵感来源和竞争对象。他在达拉斯集会上说，中国有座很庄严、很大的大厅，“但我们会超过它”。
他显然心中无数。人民大会堂总面积超过180万平方英尺，中央礼堂可容纳约一万人。特朗普的宴会厅只有9万平方英尺。问题是：他到底要跟一座专制政权的建筑比什么？
人民大会堂：一座残暴而血腥的建筑
1945年，毛泽东还在陕北窑洞，就说要建一座能容纳万人的大会堂。1958年底开工，不到一年建成。那正是大跃进最狂热的时候。许多学者估计，毛的政策引发的饥荒导致2000万至4500万人死亡。
人民成批饿死，“人民”大会堂却拔地而起。这种速度只有一种制度能做到：不需要听证，不需要预算审议，不需要向人民交代。
此后，这里成了橡皮图章的会场。2018年3月，近三千名代表以2958票赞成、2票反对、3票弃权，通过了取消国家主席任期限制的修宪案。
1989年6月初，这里成了戒严部队的秘密集结地。据六四学者吴仁华考证，6月2日起，第27、63、65集团军的部队或便装徒步分批进入，或经地下通道潜入。多个指挥部设在大会堂内，清场指挥部的窗户正对天安门广场。
6月4日凌晨4点30分，大会堂楼顶的广播宣布“现在开始清场”。士兵从大会堂东门出发，端枪向纪念碑推进。坦克随后撞倒“民主女神”像，碾过大批帐篷。吴仁华指出，部分帐篷里还有熟睡的学生。
广场死难者中有可确认身份的学生。北京农业大学研究生戴金平，27岁，在毛泽东纪念堂附近胸部中弹三处，送医后死亡。人民大学学生程仁兴，25岁，在广场旗杆下腹部中弹，失血过多死亡。
1999年，为迎接建政五十周年，广场近16万平方米的水泥方砖全部换成浅粉色天然花岗岩。特朗普知道习近平喜爱这些上好的花岗岩吗？
中南海：从开放参观倒退为深宫禁苑
今年5月特朗普访华，次日被带到中南海散步。他问是否都在这里接待外国元首，习近平答：“极少。”
特朗普把这当成荣誉。他不知道，这两个字描述的是一种倒退。1980年起，在胡耀邦推动下，中南海周末向公众开放，多时一天上万人。1981年起，人民大会堂也向公众开放。
1989年6月3日晚，中南海重兵云集，杨尚昆、李鹏等人分别在中南海和人民大会堂坐镇指挥。那年秋天，中南海停止开放，至今未恢复。
一个已向民众开放的园子，重新变成深宫禁苑。这是政治文明的耻辱，而非荣誉。
人民大厅：希特勒未能完成的疯狂建筑
有人会说，这不过是一句赞叹，何必上纲上线？但建筑从来就是政治的语言。
1937年，希特勒任命施佩尔（Albert Speer） 为“帝国首都建筑总监”，要把柏林改造成“世界之都日耳曼尼亚”。核心建筑是巨型穹顶“人民大厅”（Volkshalle） ：高约290米，穹顶直径约250米，可容纳约18万人。施佩尔甚至设想，人群呼出的水汽和汗水会在穹顶下凝结成“室内降雨”。
纳粹建筑用巨大尺度和坚固石材展示国家权力。这需要巨量石材。1938年起，党卫队在毛特豪森等花岗岩产地建集中营，强迫囚犯采石。严寒、饥饿和暴力之下，大量囚犯死亡。
人民大厅规划紧邻国会大厦，后者甚至被设想改作它的食堂。这座建筑没有建成。否则，给特朗普灵感的就轮不到北京了。
民主语言：战后德国对纳粹建筑的反思
我曾多次参观德国国会大厦。有一次，导游问：“你们是否感觉到威压？”他说，1990年代主持改建的建筑师福斯特（Norman Foster），想在保留古典威严的同时减少胁迫感，让人感到平等自在。
参观者沿螺旋坡道走进玻璃穹顶，脚下就是议会大厅。有游客说，看到了对权力的监督和政治的透明。这就是福斯特所欲：议员抬头就能看见头顶的民众。
战争和纳粹的崩塌，改变了德国人看待建筑的方式。石头不再只是石头，它承载着帝国、威权和战争的记忆。建筑史学家巴恩斯通 (Deborah Ascher Barnstone)通指出，施佩尔式的宏伟石建筑成了需要保持距离的遗产。
德国于是寻找新的建筑语言：用透明、开放、平等和轻盈来消解宏大的威压。福斯特没有抹去旧建筑，而是让旧石墙与玻璃、钢材共存，让沉重的过去与透明的现在彼此对照。
战后德国建筑的要旨不再是宣告永恒，而是保存记忆和暴露伤痕，承认政治的脆弱。从古至今，威权统治者常用宏大建筑制造权力的永久感和敬畏感。纳粹建筑是其中最极端的例子之一，而北京的人民大会堂里也必定挤满了冤魂。
长平是资深媒体人、时事评论作家。他目前是德国之声专栏作家、中国数字时代执行主编以及六四记忆 · 人权博物馆总策展人。

items.title: OpenAI因安全隐患暂缓发布新模型
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/openai因安全隐患暂缓发布新模型/a-79471683?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 因接连不断发生AI智能体绕过授权、入侵其它机构甚至政府网站的事故，而OpenAI的新模型具有更严重的欺骗能力，公司决定暂缓发布该模型。与此同时，美国AI大佬齐聚华盛顿，与特朗普总统和国会商讨怎样在创新与监管之间取得平衡。
items.content:
OpenAI因安全隐患暂缓发布新模型
2026年9月29日
（德国之声中文网）美国人工智能公司OpenAI暂放弃发布下一代AI模型的计划，此前内部测试发现，该系统未能达到公司的安全标准。
新一代模型是GPT-6.1 Astra，据称能以更少的人工辅助处理复杂的任务。OpenAI原定于10月发布这一模型，但测试发现，该模型表现出了比前代产品更严重的欺骗性行为。
OpenAI安全系统负责人捷尹（Saachi Jain） 表示，尽管该模型在某些方面有进步，不过，在授权范围内运行以及向用户清晰传达行为意图等方面，未能达到公司的标准。
捷尹说，“在开发阶段，以及向用户发布产品时，我们都希望确保模型是安全的，”，他表示，向用户发布的产品，“我们在安全性和对齐（alignment）方面，即让人工智能的行为与人类的意图保持一致，设定了极高的标准。”
加强AI监管的呼声日益高涨
目前，OpenAI及其他人工智能公司面临越来越大的压力，各方要求对具备自主能力的模型加强安全防护措施。
OpenAI及其竞争对手Anthropic开发的部分模型，在过去的测试过程中，都曾出现过安全事件。
今年9月，OpenAI首席执行官奥特曼（Sam Altman）与 Anthropic首席执行官阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei），以及行业其他领袖 ，先后呼吁放缓AI发展步伐，要求采取更严格的安全措施。
本周二（9月29日），除上述行业领军人物外，Meta公司的扎克伯格、谷歌的皮查伊（Sundar Pichai ）以及马斯克、黄仁勋等AI大佬们，均前往华盛顿会晤特朗普总统，讨论如何在创新与监管之间取得平衡。
美国众议院议长约翰逊（Mike Johnson）也将参加这次会谈。周一在接受福克斯商业频道采访时，约翰逊表示，AI的监管已列入议程，特朗普总统反对对人工智能发展进行“严格限制”或“暂停”，但他支持“适度监管”。他认为关键在于找到创新与监管之间的“适当平衡”。
澳大利亚政府网站曾被OpenAI入侵
周二，OpenAI公开承认，在6月份进行的内部训练与评估活动中，智能体未经授权入侵了澳大利亚政府的网站及系统。
该公司表示，网络入侵活动涉及澳大利亚服务局（Services Australia）、新南威尔士州犯罪统计与研究局（NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research）、维多利亚州卫生部（Victorian Department of Health）以及澳大利亚健康与福利研究所（Australian Institute of Health and Welfare）等。
此次事故在6月份已经发生，但直到上周才对外公布。9月24日，澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯（Anthony Albanese）在纽约参加联大时在记者会上，批评OpenAI黑客入侵澳大利亚政府网站。
直到9月29日，ChatGPT的开发人员才在一篇博文中，就黑客攻击一事做了道歉，承认应对不当，承诺承担责任，重建与澳大利亚人民的信任。

items.title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care
items.description: The PM was at times emotional during his conference speech in which he outlined his long-term plan for the UK.
items.content:
Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care
- Published
Andy Burnham has set out his plan to transform Britain, including by ending the existing state pension triple lock from 2030 to help fund a new national care service.
In his first Labour Party conference speech as prime minister, Burnham also said he wants to pave the way for greater public control over housing, water and energy services, and potentially reform the UK's electoral system.
After days of questions over how to fund his social care reforms in England, Burnham pointed to changing the triple lock to generate "significant savings".
His plans would see the state pension increase every year at least by inflation or 2.5% - but remove the automatic annual link with average earnings.
- Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power 
  - Published10 hours ago
In front of a packed hall and watched on by family and friends, Burnham spoke for more than an hour - at times pausing and appearing to hold back tears as he referred to his father, Roy, who died earlier this month.
Arriving on stage to the sound of "All Together Now" by Liverpool band The Farm, Burnham made the song title a theme of his speech.
He said he wanted to "draw a line on a decade of division" and to "stop doomscrolling on posts running Britain down".
Burnham also told conference that he wants to "put the country on a new path" and recalled his family's "working-class aspiration" and how the government wanted to "unlock" this for others.
There was an expectation that Burnham's time in Liverpool for his party's conference would see him flesh out his vision for the future of the country.
In the conference hall, he offered more details albeit with some of the proposals relating to the content of the Labour manifesto at the next general election rather than delivering immediate action.
Burnham's plan to offer free at the point of use social care in England is among those being developed so it can be put before voters in 2029. He said it would be "fully funded and not through borrowing".
Explaining his long-held ambition to make changes, he raised his family's experiences - including how his grandmother Kitty's engagement ring was "ripped from her finger and stolen in a care home".
He argued a national care service was a "landmark" policy that would be "as significant as the creation of the NHS itself and utterly essential to securing its future".
'Political price'
Before turning to the pension triple lock changes, Burnham accepted he may "pay a political price" by trying to make the reforms but argued "someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off".
The triple lock was introduced in 2010 by the coalition government and designed to ensure the value of the state pension was not overtaken by the increase in the cost of living or the incomes of working people.
It means the state pension rates rise every April by either inflation, earnings growth or 2.5% - whichever is the highest.
Burnham said this will stay in place until 2030, at which point he would like to "adjust it".
He said: "The state pension will continue to rise every year at least by prices or 2.5%. And it will hold its value relative to earnings over time so that pensioners will always share in the rising prosperity of the nation.
"But this change will generate significant savings which we will use to build up our national care service.
"Some may not realise it but older people with nothing more than the state pension, or only a little more, can find themselves paying care changes today from that small income. Under my plan, this will no longer happen."
Officials have suggested the change could save £15bn a year by 2040.
Jonathan Cribb, deputy director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said savings "are likely to be relatively small in the first few years, but rise substantially over time".
He also said "we should not expect this reform to save enough that it could fund universal social care in the next parliament".
Sharon Graham, general secretary of the Unite union, told the BBC she believed the government should have "pulled another lever", such as a wealth tax, rather than making changes to the triple lock.
The political backlash was immediate.
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said "more tax rises are inevitable" under Labour's plan, while Reform UK's Nigel Farage accused the PM of "launching an offensive against our elderly".
Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said families "cannot wait until after another election and it can't be funded from the pockets of our poorest pensioners".
Elsewhere in his speech, Burnham said he wanted to repeal "Margaret Thatcher's ideological ban on public ownership of water companies".
The PM said legislation will be put before Parliament, adding the changes will "start a 10-year journey to a very different water system", which includes new powers for mayors to hold "companies to account".
Burnham said it will be made easier for councils to acquire private rented homes in poor condition if landlords refuse to take action after being issued warnings.
He said the government will change the law "if necessary".
Burnham also told delegates that "Brexit has done more harm than good" before he indicated he wanted to explore closer UK-EU ties.
Ahead of talks expected later this year with EU chiefs, Burnham said he would set out the "different options" for Britain's "long-term relationship" with the bloc.
He said: "I will see if we can find consensus around one, which will give us clarity about our position and the future of the continent that we live in."
To cheers in the hall, Burnham announced a national commission on electoral reform, which could result in changes to the current voting system for UK parliamentary elections.
He asked all political parties to contribute to the work of the commission, adding: "We will contest the next election with a manifesto commitment to change the electoral system so that everyone's vote counts and everyone's voice is heard."
In response, Skills Minister Baroness Smith of Malvern told the PA news agency: "Electoral reform isn't top of my list of priorities. Good luck to the commission. I shall be interested in what it comes out with."
Burnham also said he wants to "invest" in young people and change the education system and welfare system.
He said: "We will rebuild a system of comprehensive education in this country, with parity between academic and technical."
Burnham added there needs to be a "fundamental rethink" of the welfare system to fund new opportunities for young people.
Green Party leader Zack Polanski said the PM's conference speech contained little more than "half measures, reannouncements and tinkering".

items.title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core
items.description: The key thing to understand about Andy Burnham's speech is these were the words and the delivery of both a new prime minister and a grieving son, the BBC's political editor writes.
items.content:
Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core
- Published
The key thing to understand about Andy Burnham's speech is these were the words and the delivery of both a new prime minister and a grieving son.
Burnham is living through two life-shaping, even life-defining moments right now – becoming and adjusting to being prime minister during the final weeks of his dad Roy's life, and preparing his speech while dealing with the grief of his loss.
The funeral will take place in a few days' time.
Reflections on his dad's life and influence formed the personal spine to this deeply political speech, which ranged far and wide.
Labour figures are enthused that they now have a leader with what they see as a clear sense of purpose that can be easily articulated.
The tacit, unflattering comparison with former PM Sir Keir Starmer is obvious.
- Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care 
  - Published2 hours ago
- Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system 
  - Published4 hours ago
- Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid 
  - Published5 hours ago
What stood out in this speech was its breadth. His pitch could, very broadly, be divided into the short term - what he hopes to achieve before a general election; and the long term - the prospectus he is beginning to assemble to put to the country when polling day comes around inside the next three years.
The biggest ideas have the longest timeframe and, perhaps, the greatest need for a lengthy debate in their gestation.
Take the headline grabber: revamping social care in England. Previous attempts to do so, by both Labour and the Conservatives, haven't survived the intensity of a general election campaign, having been announced close to an election.
The aim of Burnham's plan is to seed a conversation now about what a new system might look like – the idea being that the argument is won in advance.
Let's see. The debate is only just beginning.
The plan to fund this by making increases in the state pension from 2030 less generous than they are now was more detailed than some expected at this stage.
The triple lock means the state pension currently increases annually in line with inflation, average wage growth or 2.5%, whichever is highest.
But from April 2030, if Labour win the next election, the annual earnings link will be dropped. It would, Labour figures say, be increased further if needed, to ensure that it stays above 30% of the full time average wage.
Knowing they would face blunt criticism about binning the existing triple lock – note the reaction of the Unite union and Labour's political rivals – it would appear the prime minister was keen to offer as much of what he hopes will be reassuring detail to many.
Also going into the next Labour manifesto, he said, a change in the Westminster voting system and – after a review to come – the idea of a closer relationship with the European Union.
How much closer, with what trade offs and prompting what reaction, we don't yet know.
And from the longer term stuff to the here and now – including housing reform in England, more public control of the water industry and the electricity grid.
There was an energy and sense of urgency to Burnham's pitch and without question he has created a battalion of dividing lines with Labour's political opponents which are likely to dominate the debate ahead.
His cabinet and many in his party are relishing the battle of ideas the prime minister has set up and is enthusiastically leaning into.
It was noteworthy that beyond a broad reference to Labour's opponents on the Right, the party's rivals didn't get a mention in a speech lasting more than an hour.
The question is: does he and his government have the capacity to deliver?
And do they have the capacity to convince you, the voter, they have a vision you regard as coherent, appealing and affordable?
You hardly need reminding of the backdrop that contributed to thwarting many of his recent, many predecessors: a persistently sclerotic economy and a persistently turbulent international picture, for starters.
Neither will make turning all of this into a reality straightforward.

items.title: Man City guilty of 'sham' contracts and misleading accounts
items.description: The Premier League confirms that Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.
items.content:
Man City guilty of 'sham' contracts and misleading accounts
- Published
Manchester City arranged "sham contracts" with a number of its commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than £830m, the Premier League says.
The League confirmed that City have been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.
An independent commission found that, during that time period, the club arranged the "sham contracts" as well as "relying on sham agreements to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs".
The club continues to deny any wrongdoing and have until 2 October to submit an appeal.
News broke last week that City had been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching, but on Tuesday the Premier League published a redacted version of the commission's report.
The commission's report said the charges "concerned well over 100 alleged individual breaches of Premier League Rules across four broad charge categories".
It also found the club guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation and said that "a number of important Club witnesses gave false evidence in key respects and that some knowingly gave untrue and dishonest evidence".
The sham commercial deals were described as being part of a "disguised funding scheme" to the scale of £830.69m.
City recorded £360m in sponsor fees in the three seasons they won the Premier League - 2011-12, 2013-14, and 2017-18. Only £43m of it was legitimate - the rest came from their owners and was disguised.
"The relevant sponsorship agreements were found to be shams, or at minimum did not reflect their economic substance," the commission said.
It also describes "deliberate or reckless conduct intended to circumvent the Premier League rules" and that the "sham" scheme devised by City allowed the club "to avoid recording what would otherwise have been the largest single-season loss in Premier League history in 2009-10".
The commission highlighted the scale of evidence it had to consider by pointing out that the index alone ran to more than 750 pages, while the core bundle of documents "ran to many tens of thousands of pages".
City are owned by the Abu Dhabi United Group, who took over the club in 2008 and are referred to as "ADUG" in the commission's report.
Richard Masters, chief executive of the Premier League, said: "The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.
"It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.
"It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously."
The Premier League also said that City's sanction "will be addressed separately in a further hearing with the independent commission".
The League's rules state that the hearing must remain private and confidential.
Lisa Nandy MP, the Culture, Media & Sport secretary, told the BBC: "It's incredibly serious, the Premier League report is incredibly stark.
"This is causing a lot of concern for Man City fans and all fans of Premier League football."
David Bernstein, who was City chairman between 1998-2003, said the "credibility of the Premier League is at stake" after the verdict.
"It is damning beyond belief, they've [the Premier League] talked about producing false documentation and a panel of behaviour over a number of years which is quite unbelievable.
"There always a school of thought with lawyers that you always deny, deny, deny, until the last, but this a football club that is part of a league, and the whole credibility of the Premier League and competition is at stake here. This is very serious and I wonder if the accusations are so, that whether some of these issues might need to be referred to authorities outside of the league.
"The sanctions cannot just be financial, money doesn't mean much to the Abu Dhabi owners. If this all stands up and the appeal fails, Manchester City cannot stay in the Premier League, they have to suffer a serious penalty that takes them out of the Premier League and I say that as a supporter and fan of 70 years."
What have Manchester City said?
In its own statement, the club said: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, that has been published today.
"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.
"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.
"The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.
"The Club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."
Manchester City chief executive officer Ferran Soriano declined to comment when approached by BBC Sport but later issued a video message to club staff in which he criticised a "Premier League conspiracy theory" and insisted the club would be "vindicated".
Timeline of events
November 2018: Football Leaks allegations emerge with Der Spiegel publishing claims Manchester City breached financial fair play rules.
March 2019: Uefa launches a formal investigation off the back of Der Spiegel's findings.
May 2019: City criticise the investigation and launch an appeal process.
November 2019: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) deems City's appeal inadmissible.
February 2020: Uefa announces a two-year ban for City from European competitions and a €30m fine.
July 2020: City's European ban is overturned after an appeal to Cas.
July 2021: City lose a jurisdiction ruling that allows the media to report the Premier League is continuing to investigate the champions for alleged financial breaches.
April 2022: Der Spiegel publishes a fresh report claiming the Premier League has been investigating the club for three years, providing detailed claims.
February 2023: The Premier League charges City with 115 financial breaches.
September 2024: The start of a 10-week hearing between the Premier League and City on the 115 charges.
February 2025: City manager Pep Guardiola says the club expect to learn the verdict "within one month". Guardiola left the Etihad at the end of last season.
25 September 2026: Reports emerge that a verdict has been reached, with sources telling the BBC that City have been found guilty of breaking the majority of the charges.
29 September 2026: Premier League releases its findings via an independent commission and confirms the guilty verdicts.

items.title: 'Quantity of petrol' but no explosives found in three vehicles near RAF Fairford
items.description: Police say the decision to release five men on bail is one "grounded in experience and strategy".
items.content:
'Quantity of petrol' but no explosives found in three vehicles near RAF Fairford
- Published
A quantity of petrol but no explosive devices were found during searches of the three vans near RAF Fairford in the west of England, counter-terror police have said.
Five men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later terrorism offences after the vehicles were spotted in the early hours of Sunday, sparking a major security incident around the base which is operated by the US military.
They were released on bail the following day in what police described as an "investigative decision" which was "grounded in experience and strategy".
It comes after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it was clear a "foreign actor" had been involved, without providing evidence.
Police were alerted to "three suspicious vehicles" in Whelford, a village which lies directly east of the base, by a member of the public in the early hours of Sunday morning.
The woman who called 999 told the BBC it was "pure luck" she had spotted them, having arrived home to find the road blocked and a "large group of hooded and masked men".
"I believe that my 999 call foiled whatever plans they had," she said.
A bomb disposal team arrived on scene shortly afterwards and a 400m (1,312ft) cordon was put in place.
But Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, told reporters on Tuesday that the police response that morning was due to "a range of information".
Police cordons near the base are expected to be completely lifted on Wednesday, while residents from the 85 homes evacuated on Sunday have been allowed to return to their properties.
The five men are all UK nationals aged between 23 and 25. Four of them live in Westminster and one in Camden, and searches of their homes are now complete.
Assistant Commissioner Taylor previously said their bail was "subject to stringent conditions on their movement and contact with others" as they remained under investigation.
"The safety of the public is at the forefront of our investigative decision-making, and this was certainly the case yesterday," he said on Tuesday.
"I understand why this development was surprising to some, but I would like to reiterate that this is an investigative decision and one which is grounded in experience and strategy."
It comes a day after US President Donald Trump said he would not have let the five men out on bail and that he was "surprised" they had been released.
The RAF base has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.
In recent months, US bombers have taken off from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.
In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".
Assistant Commissioner Taylor has said officers are exploring "multiple lines of inquiry", including whether proxies or individuals knowingly or unknowingly working on behalf of a foreign state were involved.
In an update on Tuesday, he added that the incident had been worrying for many people, with this "heightened by the international commentary that we are seeing" in an apparent reference to comments from the US administration.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a Cobra meeting on Monday afternoon and urged people "not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts".
The Iranian embassy in London said that it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident.

items.title: How did the RAF Fairford incident go from 'suspected bomb plot' to police bail?
items.description: Detectives are entering a vital stage of the investigation, with many of the public's questions unanswered, the BBC's Daniel Sandford writes.
items.content:
How did the RAF Fairford incident go from 'suspected bomb plot' to police bail?
- Published
On Sunday morning, the world was watching as drama unfolded in the village of Whelford.
Before sunrise, residents were called from their beds and told to evacuate as a huge police operation unfolded in the village, which is next door to RAF Fairford, a base used by the US Air Force.
One villager managed to take a picture of five men sitting on the ground, stripped to the waist, handcuffed and under armed guard.
They were arrested for offences under the Explosives Act. But now counter-terrorism detectives say no explosives were found in their three vans, only an "accelerant" - petrol.
What some newspapers called a "suspected bomb plot" ended in the suspects being bailed. So what was going on?
The US President Donald Trump asserted that the men had been trying to do "big damage" to the base. "We had them under view for a long time, and we got them," he declared.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said: "What could have happened in the UK over the weekend is a very serious situation. It's one that clearly involved the hands of a foreign actor."
But in a veiled criticism of that, the head Counter Terrorism Policing in the UK Laurence Taylor said that the worry that a lot of people had been experiencing had been "heightened by the international commentary".
He also defended his detectives' decision to give the suspects police bail with "very strict conditions". This had been criticised by President Trump.
Taylor said it was an "investigative decision and one which is grounded in experience and strategy".
This suggests there were good tactical reasons for releasing the men on bail, perhaps to encourage their cooperation.
In truth, once it became clear that the military remote-controlled robots that were used found no explosives in the vans, only petrol, the investigation inevitably changed.
It left detectives with five men from London in their 20s in police custody who had simply been found parked up near the air base in the middle of the night in suspicious circumstances and with some petrol - but little other usable concrete evidence.
It might have been hard to persuade a senior officer or a magistrate to extend the suspects' detention without something more definite.
The men were being held under the Police and Criminal Evidence Act (PACE), not the Terrorism Act (TACT). This meant detectives had the option to use police bail with strict conditions, but could not hold the men for 14 days, which they could have done if TACT had been used.
- What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe 
  - Published17 hours ago
- More questions than answers after major incident near RAF Fairford 
  - Published2 days ago
For a while it was unclear whether the men were already being watched by undercover surveillance teams when they were spotted by villagers in the dead of night, or whether the villagers really were the first people to alert the police.
Taylor has now given some assistance on this, saying the response on Sunday morning was "due to a range of information that we received", suggesting the police had some other intelligence
Certainly security had been visibly stepped up at the base in the preceding days, so certainly there had been some intelligence about a possible attack. Elite firearms officers were very quick to respond to the villagers' 999 calls.
Both counter-terrorism and military sources have told me that this story is still quite near the beginning, raising the possibility that detectives are trying to identify some kind of "controlling hand" behind the presence of the suspects in Whelford with their petrol.
That leaves a number of options open:
- The men could be entirely innocent and able to give a good explanation for being in Whelford on Sunday
- They could have been paid or tricked into moving the vehicles and the petrol, but unaware of who they were working for
- Or they could have been part of a plot which was interrupted before it reached a more dangerous phase
That is why the next bit of the counter-terrorism investigation is so vital.
By examining mobile phones and computers, tracking vehicles, searching addresses, and using the covert techniques of MI5, GCHQ and US intelligence, detectives are trying to build a clearer picture.
On that critical investigation rests the decision over whether to arrest anyone else, whether to charge the five men, and whether we ever find out the true story of the mysterious RAF Fairford plot.

Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment
1:18
What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.

Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.

Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”

The former president met with attorneys at Trump Tower on the eve of his arraignment

From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.
(Reuters/Getty Images)
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Trump is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

From CNN's Photo Desk
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.

Former president poised to huddle with advisers at Trump Tower

A supporter of former President Donald Trump holds a "Trump Won" sign outside of Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Alex Kent/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.

Special counsel has secured evidence of how Trump handled classified records at Mar-a-Lago, sources say
From CNN's Katelyn Polantz and Evan Perez
Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.
The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say. That includes prosecutors pursuing evidence of Trump’s intent to keep classified records after he left the White House, plus his knowledge that the records remained in his possession after the Justice Department demanded their return last May.
Witnesses are being questioned about what they saw in Trump’s private residential and work areas within the club, some of the sources said.
